Tidy, glance and augment methods for litfit objects

Source: R/tidiers.R
litfit_tidiers.Rd

These methods return the results of a fit_litter fit as data frames, following the conventions of the broom package.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'litfit'
tidy(x, boot = NULL, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'litfit'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'litfit'
augment(x, newdata = NULL, boot = NULL, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

x

a litfit object

boot

optional litfit_bootstrap object from bootstrap_parameters for the same fit. In tidy() it adds bootstrap standard errors and percentile intervals; in augment() it adds a pointwise percentile band for the fitted curve.

conf.level

confidence level for intervals and bands (default 0.95)

...

unused

newdata

optional numeric vector of times, or a data frame with a time column, at which to predict. If omitted, the original data are returned.

Value

A data.frame.

tidy()

term, estimate; with boot also std.error, conf.low, conf.high.

glance()

model, nobs, nparams, sigma (residual standard deviation used in the likelihood), logLik, AIC, AICc, BIC, converged, time_to_50, steady_state. time_to_50 is NA if the curve never reaches 50\ steady_state can be Inf (see steady_state).

augment()

without newdata: time, mass, .fitted, .resid. With newdata: the columns of newdata (or time) plus .fitted. With boot: also .lower and .upper.

Details

  • tidy(): one row per parameter.

  • glance(): a one-row summary of the fit, including information criteria and the derived quantities time to 50\

  • augment(): the data with fitted values and residuals, or predictions at new time points, optionally with a bootstrap uncertainty band.

See also

fit_litter, bootstrap_parameters, fit_litter_all

Examples

fit <- fit_litter(
  time = pineneedles$Year, mass.remaining = pineneedles$Mass.remaining,
  model = "weibull", iters = 100, quiet = TRUE
)
tidy(fit)
#>    term estimate
#> 1  beta 3.520852
#> 2 alpha 1.092126
glance(fit)
#>     model nobs nparams      sigma   logLik       AIC      AICc       BIC
#> 1 weibull    6       2 0.05001515 9.458945 -14.91789 -10.91789 -15.33437
#>   converged time_to_50 steady_state
#> 1      TRUE   2.517099     3.405444
augment(fit)
#>        time    mass   .fitted       .resid
#> 1 0.3616438 0.97369 0.9200867  0.053603284
#> 2 0.8383562 0.84960 0.8116996  0.037900352
#> 3 1.8383562 0.58362 0.6115290 -0.027908981
#> 4 2.8356164 0.37805 0.4540819 -0.076031906
#> 5 3.8328767 0.34254 0.3338140  0.008725981
#> 6 4.8301370 0.30730 0.2435549  0.063745086

boot <- bootstrap_parameters(fit, nboot = 100)
tidy(fit, boot = boot)
#>    term estimate std.error  conf.low conf.high
#> 1  beta 3.520852 0.3378214 2.7415831  4.176179
#> 2 alpha 1.092126 0.1877691 0.7583242  1.602508
head(augment(fit, newdata = seq(0, 5, by = 0.5), boot = boot))
#>   time   .fitted    .lower    .upper
#> 1  0.0 1.0000000 1.0000000 1.0000000
#> 2  0.5 0.8881280 0.8022064 0.9374217
#> 3  1.0 0.7765261 0.6889024 0.8319859
#> 4  1.5 0.6744706 0.6024656 0.7396818
#> 5  2.0 0.5832113 0.5294072 0.6530491
#> 6  2.5 0.5025771 0.4201119 0.5758975
